reasons: Directionally correct for us as Customer (Sparkling): the edit adds a vendor-side duty to defend, settlement-control consent, prompt notice with a material-prejudice qualifier in place of the strict ten-day condition, and cooperation at Garman's expense — all pro-Customer changes with no new Customer obligations.

Rule coverage is complete: the appended paragraph adds the playbook heads (allegation-based IP infringement, Garman's breach of applicable law, unauthorized access to our data caused by Garman, gross negligence/wilful misconduct) and extends the indemnity to our affiliates, while preserving the existing procure/modify/replace remedies; notice/defence/cooperation mechanics are expressly incorporated.

Status is correctly characterised as a deviation rather than compliant: the pre-existing clause was only a warranty-breach indemnity without a defence obligation or the additional heads, so a narrow existing indemnity does not satisfy the rule.

The failed 'minimal edit p0090' check (0.827 changed ratio) is an artefact of inserting two sentences into a long single paragraph; the original warranty and remedy language is preserved verbatim and only the ten-day notice condition was substituted, which is the smallest edit that reaches the playbook position.
Comment is accurate, concise, in the required voice with the [Playbook] prefix, explains what changed and why, and offers the 3x annual fees super-cap fallback.
